speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; please tell me, when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of forceful vomiting, retching, choking, and subsequent chest pain in a patient with a recent history of Lyme disease is highly suggestive of a specific complication. Can you describe the nature of the pain, specifically if it is sharp and worsens when you take a deep breath? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms a large retrosternal mediastinal air collection. Based on your history of forceful retching followed by choking and severe chest pain, I suspect a Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). I need to confirm this with a contrast study and check your blood work immediately. REQUEST TEST: Serum_amylase, Serum_lipase, CBC, Chemistry_panel; REQUEST IMAGES: Contrast_esophagram
